messages:
maya (product): Quick sync — need to lock streaming semantics for chat/completions before next sprint planning. Scope: decide SSE vs WebSocket for public API, choose delta payload shape (minimal text vs token-level + metadata), define `finish_reason` values, and set launch gates (SDK changes, mobile resume, enterprise audit needs). Who has objections to picking pragmatic defaults and iterating?
liam (eng-runtime): +1 to pragmatic defaults. My take: start with SSE for hosted public endpoints — easier infra, HTTP-friendly (proxies, CDNs). WS when we need bidi or persistent sessions (private/dedicated customers can opt-in).
olivia (eng-ml): Agree on SSE-first. For delta schema, recommend a compact envelope that supports evolution. Example deltas we can support:
```json
{"delta_type":"tokens","content":"hello","token_index":0,"final":false}
{"delta_type":"text","content":" world","final":true,"finish_reason":"stop"}
```
We should include optional `token_index` and `logprob` later, but not in v1.
raj (devex): SDK side: map each server event to an SDK callback: onDelta, onFinish, onError. Please standardize `finish_reason` enum early — SDKs will hardcode it. Proposed values: `stop`, `max_tokens`, `cancel`, `error`. Keep names lowercase and stable.
sara (customer-success): FYI: Two enterprise pilots asked for deterministic finish reasons and a reconnect/resume story (audit + long-running sessions for agents). They will push for resume-by-KV-cache or sequence-id. Important for compliance customers.
liam (eng-runtime): Resume is the hard part. For SSE we can support resume by assigning a session_id + last_event_id and replaying KV cache from the same model checkpoint if within a short TTL. For long resumes we'd need persistent session state (storage) — reserve for Dedicated/Private.
olivia (eng-ml): On finish semantics: distinguish between model-internal stop vs user-cancel. `finish_reason` should be emitted on the final delta event and also as a separate `finish` event so SDKs can rely on a single callback.
raj (devex): Agreed — final event + explicit `finish` event. Also include a `partial: true|false` flag on final if we truncated due to `max_tokens` so logs are clear.
maya (product): Narrowing possible launch plan: v1 (hosted public API) = SSE, lightweight delta (text + delta_type + optional ids), finish_reason enum as above, SDK callback mapping, no resume (= soft failure for reconnects). v2 = WebSocket option, token-level deltas, resume and persistent sessions for Dedicated/private. Any blockers?
sara (customer-success): Some pilot customers will accept v1 if we commit to v2 timeline (8–12 weeks). Please capture in roadmap.
liam (eng-runtime): Blockers: need server-side backpressure semantics defined (how we signal pause/resume to client) and infra metrics (per-token latency). For SSE we can use `x-stream-status` events; for WS use opcodes.
olivia (eng-ml): Also call out safety: partial deltas might reveal low-confidence tokens; include optional `confidence` later but we should document current behavior (no logprobs in v1).
raj (devex): Actionable SDK work: map SSE `event: delta` and `event: finish` to onDelta/onFinish. Add a transitory flag when reconnect happens.
deply-bot: deploy-bot: rollout-checklist created: checklist/streaming-sse-v1 -> 6 items (spec doc, SDK PRs, canary config, metrics dashboards, docs, legal review).
maya (product): Concrete decisions captured: 1) SSE-first public v1, WS as v2+; 2) delta envelope minimal text-first (see Olivia example); 3) finish_reason enum = [stop, max_tokens, cancel, error]; 4) v1 no resume; v2 resume/persistent sessions for Dedicated; 5) Launch gates: SDKs (node/py/js mobile), docs + examples, canary with 2 pilot customers, perf dashboards.
maya (product): Next steps — owners: liam (runtime) = infra + backpressure spec, olivia (ml) = delta schema doc + examples, raj (devex) = SDK mapping PRs, sara (cs) = confirm pilot acceptance and timeline. Please ack with :eyes: and any concerns by EOD tomorrow.
